doc.title: Maria Schneider interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Hobbies, Janet Lynn, Gil Evans and a rich life
summary: She describes outside interests, childhood ice skating, her overwhelming first meeting with Gil Evans, and that music is fed by a rich life.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Do you have hobbies now that provide some part away from music for you?

Um, yeah, interests. Some interests. I mean now I’ve gotten all excited about astronomy again. I want to buy a telescope. I’m interested in Chi Gong and some kind of martial arts kinds of things. You know I like to read, I like to ride bikes, for years I loved dance, I love to go see dance. I’d like to take Flamenco dancing. I haven’t done it, but I’d like to. It’s just a matter of being in town enough to do it. Because I love Flamenco music. And that’s another thing that’s maybe going to be the result of having a manager is just taking more time to do those things. Because all those things, you know when I was a child, I think this is the other thing that’s powerful about when you’re younger and why I like to go back to the feeling of what it was when I made music as a child. Because when I was a child music was very important and nobody ever had to ask me to practice. I practiced constantly and I loved to play. But everything that I did I did with the same degree of passion that I did music. When I ice skated I was just, I was so passionate about that. And I have the whole dress and the business, and we did ice skating shows and I remember the first time I saw Janet Lynn skate in a skating show. And she came towards me. I was sitting in like the third row. And when she came on the ice and came towards me I was so excited that she as like flying all through the air. It was like my vision just went nuts. And I look to Janet Lynn in the same way — and the only other time that ever happened to me in my life is when I met Gil Evans. He came walking towards me and I got so freaked out that my visual field, I must — something must have optically started spazzing out behind my eye. Because he was flying through the air and I couldn’t catch him. And I was thinking this was what happened to me exactly with seeing Janet Lynn skate. You know? But then, so I loved her to the degree I loved Gil Evans. And now, you know, I miss getting into things with the same degree of passion that I do music. Because music isn’t enough for me in life. There’s other things too. And I love music but I think what I love about music is it’s a valve for other things. I love life, and I want more time to live. And to me music is, one of the problems with musicians is I think they get so caught up in making records and going to the next project that very often the person’s first record is the most powerful. Because that record represents years of just working on your own and

doing other things in life, and then suddenly you become so busy doing your music you aren’t paying attention so much to the other things in your life because they aren’t as important as the music. But what feeds the music? Music is fed by a deep and rich life. So I think it’s really important to have other things in your life that you can do with equal love.
